##### Double Exponential Distribution {#sec-eda-double-exponential-distribution}

**Probability Density Function**

The general formula for the [probability density function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$f(x) = \frac{e^{-\left|\frac{x - \mu}{\beta}\right|}}{2\beta}$$

where $\mu$ is the [location parameter](#sec-eda-location-and-scale-parameters) and $\beta$ is the [scale parameter](#sec-eda-location-and-scale-parameters). The case where $\mu = 0$ and $\beta = 1$ is called the **standard double exponential distribution**. The equation for the standard double exponential distribution is

$$f(x) = \frac{e^{-|x|}}{2}$$

Since the general form of probability functions can be [expressed in terms of the standard distribution](#sec-eda-location-and-scale-parameters), all subsequent formulas in this section are given for the standard form of the function.

Note that the double exponential distribution is also commonly referred to as the Laplace distribution.

The following is the plot of the double exponential probability density function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-pdf
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential probability density function"
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

ddexp <- function(x) exp(-abs(x)) / 2

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(y = ddexp(x)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "f(x)") +
  theme_light()
```

**Cumulative Distribution Function**

The formula for the [cumulative distribution function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$F(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^{x}}{2} & \text{for } x < 0 \\[4pt] 1 - \dfrac{e^{-x}}{2} & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}$$

The following is the plot of the double exponential cumulative distribution function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-cdf
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential cumulative distribution function"
pdexp <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, exp(x) / 2, 1 - exp(-x) / 2)

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(y = pdexp(x)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "F(x)") +
  theme_light()
```

**Percent Point Function**

The formula for the [percent point function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$G(p) = \begin{cases} \log(2p) & \text{for } p \le 0.5 \\ -\log(2(1 - p)) & \text{for } p > 0.5 \end{cases}$$

The following is the plot of the double exponential percent point function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-ppf
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential percent point function"
qdexp <- function(p) ifelse(p <= 0.5, log(2 * p), -log(2 * (1 - p)))

tibble(p = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(x = qdexp(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(p, x)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = expression(alpha), y = expression(G(alpha))) +
  theme_light()
```

**Hazard Function**

The formula for the [hazard function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$h(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^{x}}{2 - e^{x}} & \text{for } x < 0 \\[4pt] 1 & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}$$

The following is the plot of the double exponential hazard function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-hazard
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential hazard function"
hdexp <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, exp(x) / (2 - exp(x)), 1)

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(y = hdexp(x)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "h(x)") +
  theme_light()
```

**Cumulative Hazard Function**

The formula for the [cumulative hazard function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$H(x) = \begin{cases} -\log\!\left(1 - \dfrac{e^{x}}{2}\right) & \text{for } x < 0 \\[4pt] x + \log(2) & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}$$

The following is the plot of the double exponential cumulative hazard function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-cumulative-hazard
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential cumulative hazard function"
hdexp_cum <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, -log(1 - exp(x) / 2), x + log(2))

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(y = hdexp_cum(x)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "H(x)") +
  theme_light()
```

**Survival Function**

The formula for the [survival function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$S(x) = \begin{cases} 1 - \dfrac{e^{x}}{2} & \text{for } x < 0 \\[4pt] \dfrac{e^{-x}}{2} & \text{for } x \ge 0 \end{cases}$$

The following is the plot of the double exponential survival function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-survival
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential survival function"
sdexp <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, 1 - exp(x) / 2, exp(-x) / 2)

tibble(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(y = sdexp(x)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "x", y = "S(x)") +
  theme_light()
```

**Inverse Survival Function**

The formula for the [inverse survival function](#sec-eda-related-distributions) of the double exponential distribution is

$$Z(p) = \begin{cases} \log(2(1 - p)) & \text{for } p \le 0.5 \\ -\log(2p) & \text{for } p > 0.5 \end{cases}$$

The following is the plot of the double exponential inverse survival function.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-double-exponential-dist-inverse-survival
#| fig-cap: "Standard double exponential inverse survival function"
zdexp <- function(p) ifelse(p <= 0.5, log(2 * (1 - p)), -log(2 * p))

tibble(p = seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(z = zdexp(p)) |>
  ggplot(aes(p, z)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = expression(alpha), y = expression(Z(alpha))) +
  theme_light()
```

**Common Statistics**

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| Mean | $\mu$ |
| Median | $\mu$ |
| Mode | $\mu$ |
| Range | $-\infty$ to $\infty$ |
| Standard Deviation | $\sqrt{2}\beta$ |
| Coefficient of Variation | $\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{\beta}{\mu}\right)$ |
| Skewness | 0 |
| Kurtosis | 6 |

**Parameter Estimation**

The maximum likelihood estimators of the location and scale parameters of the double exponential distribution are

$$\hat{\mu} = \tilde{X}$$

$$\hat{\beta} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}|X_{i} - \tilde{X}|}{N}$$

where $\tilde{X}$ is the sample median.

**Software**

Some general purpose statistical software programs support at least some of the probability functions for the double exponential distribution.
